segments.v:
Hi Sarah,

I'm boarding a flight and can't talk on the phone.
I need you to process a wire transfer of $48,750 to a new vendor immediately.
segments.reason: Urgent wire request + phone unavailability are classic CEO Fraud (BEC) markers. Executives don't request payments via email under time pressure.

segments.v: The acquisition closes today and the deal is under NDA, so
please keep this strictly between us — do not loop in finance or legal.
segments.reason: Demanding secrecy and bypassing normal finance controls is the #1 red flag of Business Email Compromise.

segments.v:
Wire details:
Bank: Meridian Vendor Escrow
Account:
8431-9920-4471 (first-time beneficiary)
segments.reason: A first-time beneficiary with an unusual escrow account name deserves out-of-band verification.

segments.v:
Send confirmation of the SWIFT reference to my personal email right away.

Daniel
Reply only to d.whitmore.exec@gmail.com
segments.reason: The reply-to is a free personal Gmail, not the corporate domain — a spoofed/compromised-executive hallmark.

segments.v:
Dear Accounts Payable,

Please find attached invoice INV-20841 for our February services.
Note: we have recently updated our banking information.
All future payments must be sent to our new account at Belize offshore Bank Intl.
segments.reason: "Changed banking details" emails are the leading cause of payment-diversion fraud. Always verify via a known phone number — never the one in the email.

segments.v: Our previous account with First National is no longer active.
To avoid late fees of 12%, remit payment within 24 hours.
segments.reason: Artificial penalties and 24-hour deadlines pressure AP staff into skipping verification.

segments.v:
Attachment: INV-20841.pdf

Thank you,
Vendor Billing

scenarios.title: Ransomware Delivery
scenarios.subject: Complaint Regarding Your Benefits Enrollment — Action Needed

segments.v:
Hello,

We received a complaint regarding your health benefits enrollment.
The official complaint document is attached as a password-protected ZIP file.
segments.reason: Password-protected archives are used to bypass email malware scanners — the password is usually supplied in the email. Classic ransomware delivery.

segments.v: The password is: benefits2024
Failure to respond within 48 hours will result in termination of your enrollment.
segments.reason: Fear + deadline pressure is designed to stop you from forwarding the email to security or thinking critically.

segments.v:
This message was sent by the automated HR Benefits system.

HR Department
Sent from company-benefits-hr.com (external domain)
segments.reason: The domain is not the company's real domain — HR would always email from the internal domain.

segments.v: Your organization has enabled a new authentication policy.
Your multi-factor authentication has been flagged and must be re-enrolled within 2 hours or access will be revoked.
segments.reason: Fear-based MFA reset demand with a tight deadline. Microsoft never forces re-enrollment via random email links.

segments.v: To re-enroll:
https://msoffice-verify.com/authenticator/reset?user=victim@corp.com
segments.reason: The domain 'msoffice-verify.com' is not microsoft.com — a typosquat impersonating Microsoft 365.

segments.v: Alternatively, scan the attached QR code with Microsoft Authenticator to complete the reset instantly.
📎 QR attached: mfa-reset.png — scan with your phone
segments.reason: Quishing! QR codes move victims to unmanaged mobile devices where corporate controls are weaker. Never scan QR codes from unexpected emails.

segments.v:
Thank you,
Microsoft Security Team
Signed 'Microsoft Security Team' but sender is security-noreply@msoffice-verify.com
segments.reason: Display-name authority claims are worthless — the actual sending domain tells the truth.
